prohibitions: Never create, update, complete or delete tasks
guide.summary: Use Todoist OAuth with the read-only data:read scope. Register the app and configure a redirect URI, then test individual-account authorization and a read-only tasks request with cursor pagination. Write, delete and team-administration scopes are excluded. Provider review and multi-workspace distribution requirements are not documented in the supplied sources and remain unknown.

findings.title: Authorization code flow with a scope parameter is documented
findings.detail: The documented authorization URL takes client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. The app redirects the user to that URL.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: Request data:read for listing tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. It matches the read-only task listing use case.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles through the tasks endpoint

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Do not request write or delete scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write and data:delete grant modification or deletion. They are excluded by the read-only prohibition and must not be requested.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Redirect URI must be configured in the App Management Console
findings.detail: Authorization fails if the redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console. Configure it before the authorization test.

evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

findings.title: The connecting user can deny authorization
findings.detail: If the user denies the request, Todoist redirects to the configured redirect URI with error=access_denied. The test must handle this path.

evidence.quote: When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .
User Rejected Authorization Request

steps.title: Register the app and configure its redirect URI
steps.detail: Create the app in the App Management Console and add the callback URL used by your test implementation. Record the client ID and secret in your secret store.
steps.doneWhen: The app exists in the console with the callback URL saved and the client credentials stored outside source control.

evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.

steps.title: Implement authorization URL and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect with scope=data:read, a state value and response_type=code. Prepare the callback handler and token exchange. Do not execute the flow yet.
steps.doneWhen: The code builds the authorization URL with scope data:read and includes a callback handler for the code parameter.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Authorize your own individual Todoist test account
steps.detail: Sign in with your individual test account and approve the data:read request. Confirm the callback receives a code, then exchange it for an access token. Test denial separately if needed.
steps.doneWhen: The callback receives an authorization code and the token exchange returns an access token for the test account.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
User Rejected Authorization Request

steps.title: Test the first page of task listing
steps.detail: Call the tasks endpoint with the token and a limit. Expected response includes a results array and next_cursor. Boundary check: this is a GET request only; confirm the request log shows no POST, PUT, DELETE or other write, and that tasks are unchanged.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns results and next_cursor, with only GET requests in the request log.

evidence.quote: get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

steps.title: Test cursor pagination for task listing
steps.detail: Request the next page with the same parameters and the next_cursor value from step 4. Expected response: a results array with a new next_cursor or none. Boundary check: confirm GET only in the request log, with no task changes.
steps.doneWhen: The second page returns results using the cursor and the request log shows only GET requests.

evidence.quote: curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
